title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 4: - Coach Kyle Shanahan came out on the field before team drills today at roughly 10:45 and staying through the end. At one point, he was even watching from next to a big speaker in the end zone. It was the longest he's been on the field during an open practice yet. - This was the first fully padded practice of camp and, perhaps to no one's surprise, the physicality ramped up. That happened despite Chris Foerster's message in the team meeting about not fighting and protecting one another. - The biggest scuffle came late in practice when LB Fred Warner took exception with TE Jake Tonges seemingly pushing off to get open. Tonges made the catch and though he was flagged for OPI, Warner ran over to him to let him know he didn't like it. OT Colton McKivitz got involved then Dre Greenlaw took him to the ground and the whole team surrounded them. It was broken up soon after but was not what Foerster was hoping to see. - A handful of plays before that, Greenlaw shoved RB Christian McCaffrey to the ground on the sideline with McCaffrey getting up and shoving him. Greenlaw seemed to realize quickly that wasn't a good idea given CMC's importance and did not retaliate so nothing came of it, though it's fair to say that could have still been on the minds of both sides for the rest of that team period. - WR Deebo Samuel was not yet at practice today. He's expected to get everything signed and squared away today and could be out there as soon as Saturday. All signs point toward him being back in his No. 19 with Jacob Cowing switching to No. 6. - No update on WR Ricky Pearsall's knee injury just yet.
